practice_description.medium: Reading groups, publishing, events, study infrastructure, web platforms
practice_description.practice_summary: Trust is a Berlin-based collective that builds knowledge commons and study infrastructure as creative practice. They organize reading groups, workshops, and publishing projects that treat collective learning as a form of cultural production.
practice_description.methodology: Trust operates through sustained collective study — organizing reading groups, discussion series, and collaborative publishing projects. Their methodology treats the infrastructure of learning itself (how groups form, how knowledge circulates, how discussions are structured) as design material. They build both social protocols (formats for gathering and study) and technical infrastructure (web platforms, publishing tools) to support distributed knowledge production.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Trust's practice of designing study infrastructure as creative medium directly models how A(DAI)'s knowledge commons could function as both operational infrastructure and exhibited artwork in a graph-curated setting.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: In an expanded sense, yes. The knowledge outputs — publications, discussion archives, reading lists — can serve as substrate material. The study infrastructure itself is a kind of conceptual substrate for community formation.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes. Trust's practice is fundamentally relational — knowledge emerges from connections between texts, participants, and ideas. The reading group format is a social graph that produces meaning through connections.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: The collective's output evolves through ongoing programs and community engagement. Reading groups generate new connections and reframe earlier material. The knowledge commons is continuously recomposed through new inquiry.

works.title: Trust Reading Groups
works.description: Ongoing series of collectively organized reading groups on topics spanning technology, philosophy, politics, and ecology. Each series is carefully designed with curated reading lists and structured discussion formats.
works.relevance: Models how structured collective study can be a creative practice. The curatorial work of selecting texts and designing discussion formats mirrors A(DAI)'s graph curation.

works.title: Relearn
works.description: A recurring self-organized learning event/summer school exploring alternatives to conventional education, often involving Trust members. Participants propose and lead sessions on technology, art, and politics.
works.relevance: Demonstrates decentralized, commons-based learning infrastructure. The self-organizing format models how A(DAI)'s community might contribute to and reshape the knowledge graph.

works.title: Trust Publications and Web Presence
works.description: Web-based publishing projects documenting reading groups, discussions, and collective research outputs. The website itself is a designed knowledge commons.
works.relevance: Shows how web infrastructure can embody commons values while functioning as a persistent, navigable knowledge resource.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Trust treats the design of study protocols, gathering formats, and knowledge infrastructure as creative practice. The rules and structures that govern how people come together to learn are designed with the same intentionality as artworks.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Study infrastructure including reading group formats, web-based knowledge commons, collaborative learning protocols, event formats for collective inquiry.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Deeply commons-oriented. Trust exists to build and maintain knowledge commons. Their infrastructure is designed to be non-extractive, collectively governed, and openly accessible. They are one of the key nodes in Berlin's commons-based cultural infrastructure.

governance_model.governance_detail: Collective governance among core members with distributed decision-making. Reading groups are often facilitated by different participants. The organizational structure is intentionally flat and non-hierarchical. [uncertain]

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Participation is voluntary. The collective study format inherently involves ongoing consent through presence and contribution. No surveillance or tracking of participants.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collective authorship for publications. Individual contributions within reading groups are acknowledged but the emphasis is on collectively produced knowledge.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Trust's practice is durational and ongoing. Reading groups meet regularly, each series building on and reframing earlier inquiries. The knowledge commons grows accretively over years of sustained practice.

data_materiality.data_sources: Published texts (books, articles, essays), participant contributions and discussion notes, collectively generated notes and syntheses.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Ethically sourced — published works cited with attribution, self-generated discussion material, participant contributions given with informed consent.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Not directly engaged with computational embedding spaces. However, their practice of mapping connections between texts and ideas is conceptually adjacent to semantic space navigation at a human-curated scale.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Primarily textual and sonic (discussion), with some visual elements in web publishing.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Primary encounter is through in-person reading groups in Berlin and the web-based publishing platform. Events sometimes hosted at art spaces and cultural venues. The gathering itself is the primary spatial form.

interoperability.composability: Moderate. Published outputs are openly accessible. Reading lists and discussion summaries could be integrated into other knowledge systems. The formats and protocols they design could be adopted by other communities.
interoperability.technical_openness: Open access, formats are replicable and forkable

technical_approach.stack: Web technologies, collaborative document tools, mailing lists, lightweight publishing infrastructure designed for sustainability and accessibility

network_position.scene_affiliation: Berlin independent culture, free/open-source culture, post-digital art, critical technology community, European commons movement.
network_position.connections: 0xSalon (shared Berlin knowledge commons scene), Constant (Brussels, shared commons/study ethos), Relearn network, broader European independent cultural infrastructure

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Trust's decade-long practice of building study infrastructure as creative practice is a direct precedent for A(DAI). They could partner on designing the social protocols that accompany A(DAI)'s technical infrastructure — how communities gather around a knowledge graph. Their experience with sustained collective study provides lessons for A(DAI)'s long-term community building.
